summary.title: Command Line Interface Guidelines
summary.one_liner: You learn open-source best practices for designing command-line programs, covering UNIX-inspired principles, help text, exit codes, stdout/stderr use, and error suggestions.
takeaways: Use a command-line argument parsing library so flags, help text and spelling suggestions are handled consistently.
Return zero on success and non-zero on failure, and send primary output to stdout while routing logs and errors to stderr.
Show concise help by default and extensive help for -h and --help, leading with examples.
Suggest corrections for invalid input when you can guess the intent, but don't force the change on the user, since guessing can be dangerous.
summary.summary: This open-source guide, written by Aanand Prasad, Ben Firshman, Carl Tashian and Eva Parish, updates traditional UNIX principles for modern command-line programs. It starts with philosophy (human-first design, composability, consistency, saying just enough, discoverability, conversational interaction, robustness, and empathy) and then gives concrete guidelines grouped into essential basics and nice-to-have rules. Examples are drawn from tools such as jq, git, and heroku to show good help output and conventions. The page shown is the opening portion, so the documentation section is cut off partway through.
